subject: Dedicated capacity scoping for Converso: traffic & prompt profile
messages:
From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@orionai.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@orionai.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 17:03:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated capacity scoping for Converso pilot

Hi Priya,

Thanks for taking this — we’re excited to explore Redwood Dedicated for our Converso product. We have an upcoming pilot (internal launch in Q4) and need guidance on sizing: concurrent sessions, burst tolerance, and expected GPU footprint. Quick summary: 

- Current expected steady-state QPS (prompts/sec): 18
- Peak burst QPS (short spikes during marketing events): 280 for ~7 minutes
- Typical session concurrency (simultaneous open sessions per end-user): 1
- Active conversational sessions (end-users generating requests): ~2,400 at peak across region (estimated)
- Prompt sizes: average 140 tokens (user prompt + system preprocessing)
- Response sizes: average 380 tokens (mostly long-form answers)
- Expected model: open-llama-70b variant (we may try a quantized 4-bit build)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 550ms generation-only, p99 < 1.2s ideally
- Want to avoid tail latency spikes that degrade UX; we expect burst traffic orientation to be regional (us-east primary)

I attached a CSV export of a week of production traffic we used to estimate these numbers (orionai_traffic_export.csv). Can you send over your recommended sizing template and a short checklist of the key unknowns we should clarify on our side? Also happy to schedule a 30-minute technical sync this week.

Thanks,

Maya Singh
Product Ops Manager, OrionAI
maya.singh@orionai.com

Attachment: orionai_traffic_export.csv (csv)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <maya.singh@orionai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 17:46:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity scoping for Converso pilot

Hi Maya — thanks for the great summary and for the CSV. Looping in Ben (sales engineering) and Avery (solutions) so we can cover both the sizing math and the deployment tradeoffs.

I’ve attached our Dedicated sizing template (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx) — it’s intentionally short: please fill the green cells if you can. The high-level unknowns that materially change sizing are:

- Model variant & quantization (70B fp16 vs 4-bit quantized)
- Average and p99 sequence length (tokens) for both prompt + response combined
- Ratio of streaming vs non-streaming responses (streaming increases concurrency costs)
- Stateful conversational sessions vs stateless requests (how long do KV caches need to live)
- Regional affinity and tolerance for cross-region fallback (do you require single-region only?)

Suggested next steps:
1) Fill the template and drop it back to me (or we can pull values during the call).
2) 30-min sync — proposed slots: Wed 10:00–10:30am ET or Thu 3:00–3:30pm ET. Which works for you?

Quick note on attachments: we prefer the CSV + a sample of raw prompts (anonymized) so we can calibrate tokenization patterns.

Cheers,

Priya Natarajan
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@orionai.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 19:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity scoping for Converso pilot

Priya / Maya — quick follow from the infra side with the things I’ll need to produce a conservative GPU footprint estimate: 

- Clarify model build: is the 70B you mentioned a full fp16 build or do you already plan to run a quantized variant? If undecided, provide both examples.
- Can you provide p50/p90/p99 sequence length (tokens) for response alone, not just averages? p99 response length drives memory/KV cache pressure.
- Are there long-running sessions that keep KV cache populated for minutes? If yes, what’s p90 session duration?
- Do you have a hard latency SLO per customer tier? Example: free-tier p95 < 1.0s, paid p95 < 0.5s.
- Do you expect synchronous tools/function calls during generation (which can extend end-to-end latency)?

A couple of internal notes I’ll run in parallel: I’ll simulate a burst curve based on the CSV, then run slot estimation for a 70B fp16 and a 70B 4-bit quantized build. If we need to hit p99 < 1.2s under 280 QPS bursts, we’ll likely recommend a baseline pool of reserved GPUs plus a modest warm burst pool; details after I run the numbers.

On logistics — Maya, either proposed sync time works for me; leaning Wednesday. Please pick one and I’ll block calendar once you confirm.

—Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks — all, confirmed Wed 10:00am ET works for us. A few answers inline below to help your initial pass: 

- Model: planning for 70B fp16 for quality tests, and a 4-bit quantized fallback for cost testing. Please size both.
- Response lengths (tokens): p50 280, p90 510, p99 1,020 (these are from sampled logs)
- Session behavior: ~75% of interactions are short-lived (single turn). The remaining 25% are multi-turn sessions with p90 duration ~12 minutes, p99 ~22 minutes.
- Streaming: ~60% of responses are streamed to clients.
- Latency SLO: we want paid customers p95 < 500ms generation time; enterprise pilot cohort can tolerate p95 < 750ms.
- Tools: we make synchronous API calls to a retrieval layer ~18% of the time during generation.

I’ve uploaded an anonymized sample of raw prompts and a sanitized token histogram to the Drive link in the metadata — should help with tokenization edge-cases. Looking forward to the call.

Best,

Maya
Product Ops Manager, OrionAI
maya.singh@orionai.com
